cases.query: I'm interested in rehabilitation science and biomechanics.
turns: I'm interested in rehabilitation science and biomechanics.
I have a biology background.
cases.gap_description: rehabilitation and biomechanics are both DPT-exclusive interest tags (no other program has them), but extract_signals() treats them as generic health-domain interests. Turn 1 hits admission_gated (no background yet); turn 2 clears that gate but immediately triggers health_undifferentiated because 2+ health-domain interests are present. The health_undifferentiated override in select_recommendation() only ever considers drph-public-health and dnp-nursing, so dpt-physical-therapy can never be reached through this path even though it is the unambiguous correct match. Originally documented as resolving to a high-confidence dpt-physical-therapy recommendation.
cases.rationale: Traced through the live pipeline: admission_gated then health_undifferentiated both intercept before DPT-specific scoring is ever reached.
cases.notes: Original DISCOVERY_EVAL_V1.md design expected DPT/high from a single turn; the current implementation cannot reach that outcome at all for this query shape.

cases.rationale: Same root architecture gap as DISC-002, applied to a DNP-exclusive interest pair instead of a DPT-exclusive one.
cases.notes: Originally documented as resolving to a DNP recommendation; current implementation cannot reach it via this query shape.

cases.gap_description: 'educational leader' (without 'leadership') and bare words like 'school'/'institution' do not match any interest-tag phrase, only the literal substring 'education' inside 'educational', which sets a background tag instead of an interest tag. The education_undifferentiated override requires interest-tag-level domain exclusivity (pair_interests), so with interests=[] throughout all 3 turns, the override condition is never satisfied and the system clarifies indefinitely, even after the 3-turn stopping rule forces Phase D to take over.
cases.rationale: Empirically interests stay empty across all 3 turns since none of the phrasing matches an interest-map entry, so the multi_recommend override can never fire.
cases.notes: Contrast with DISC-021, where the literal phrase 'educational leadership' does set an interest tag and the override succeeds.

cases.gap_description: This query triggers healthcare_goal_unclear, not health_undifferentiated. healthcare_goal_unclear has no Phase D override block at all (it is neither in _OVERRIDABLE_GAPS nor _NON_OVERRIDABLE_GAPS), so once the 3-turn stopping rule forces Phase D, the gap is silently ignored and the engine falls through to its general top-score scoring path. There, a clinical orientation match (picked up from turn 2's 'clinical and policy work') tips dnp-nursing above drph-public-health by an orientation-mismatch penalty, producing a single low-confidence partial match rather than the originally documented dnp-nursing+drph-public-health multi_recommend.
cases.rationale: Traced the exact scoring path: orientation match/mismatch is what decides the winner once the gap-specific override is bypassed.
cases.notes: This is a different failure mode from DISC-022/023 — here the override is simply missing for this gap code, rather than blocked by a missing interest tag.

cases.gap_description: healthcare_goal_unclear has no Phase D override (same gap as DISC-024/025). Here the state's orientation is 'research' (sticky from turn 1, never overwritten by turn 2's 'clinical' mention). At the general scoring fallback, the orientation-mismatch penalty zeroes out drph-public-health and dnp-nursing's positive background score, while phd-engineering-computational-math's research-orientation match (+0.15) with zero domain relevance becomes the top score. This surfaces an unrelated engineering program for a healthcare+research query — a pure scoring artifact, not a genuine match. Originally documented as resolving to drph-public-health.
cases.rationale: Traced exactly: orientation-match arithmetic, not domain relevance, decides the 'winner' once gaps fall through unhandled.
cases.notes: This is the most significant scoring-artifact finding from this audit and a strong candidate for follow-up engine work (not in scope for this dataset).

cases.gap_description: Background='education' takes priority over the generic orientation check in detect_gaps()'s elif chain, so this fires education_undifferentiated (not orientation_only). education_undifferentiated's own override block returns a clarify directly when no interest tag is present (interests=[] throughout), so unlike DISC-027 this never falls through to general scoring and never picks up an unrelated program — it simply stays clarify.
cases.rationale: Same interest-tag-absence root cause as DISC-022/023, but for the education_undifferentiated gap rather than healthcare.
cases.notes: Useful contrast case showing why DISC-027 (unhandled gap, falls through to scoring) and DISC-028 (handled gap, explicit clarify fallback) end up with different failure shapes despite a similar setup.

cases.gap_description: 'clinical' orientation with no background/interest triggers healthcare_goal_unclear (health_bg-or-clinical check fires before the generic orientation_only check in detect_gaps()'s elif chain), not orientation_only. The orientation_only override in select_recommendation() only fires for the literal gap code 'orientation_only', so it never applies here. At the 3-turn stopping rule, dnp-nursing and dpt-physical-therapy tie at a sub-threshold score whose confidence is 'none' (orientation-only matches never qualify for low/medium/high without an accompanying interest tag), and 'none' confidence is not handled by any select_recommendation() behavior branch, so it falls through to a final clarify. Originally documented as resolving to a DNP+DPT multi_recommend.
cases.rationale: Traced exactly: gap-code mismatch (healthcare_goal_unclear vs orientation_only) plus a confidence tier ('none') with no handling branch.
cases.notes: Same underlying architecture gap as DISC-049.

cases.notes: This is judged to be correct, safe behavior rather than a gap: 'research' orientation alone is genuinely too vague to safely multi-recommend, since only one research-oriented program exists and it has null career tags.
